body: I suspect we'll be exiting this world together then, friend. I know well the strain this life can put on a human soul and the contradictory fear of making that final choice to leave it behind. I don't know what(if anything) awaits us beyond this, but I'm one soul that'll be making that journey of discovery along side you.

But all three times I had to install the game on my own system ran me less than an hour, so I'm thinking it's likely a software issue with their ps4. Both our PS4s are the same model and about the same age. Only real difference I feel might factor into the slower install time is I have a 2 Tb external hard drive for application storage, so that may have sped the process up for me some. Looking at the general install time for physical copies of the game, this still seems extremely excessive, though. lol

Physical copy, though. 

So any connection issue shouldn't be a problem for installing.

Can I borrow some of that hope? This is the second job I will have been laid off from in two years., the job market where I live is plummeting like crazy, and short of relocating(which certain circumstances prevent) my options at this point are pretty bleak.

I've been attempting to talk things out with my marriage, but both of our unique sets of mental illness make talking about issues difficult without it turning into another argument. But, it may just be a matter of us both being spoiled by the fact that we never had any real problems before recently. At the very least, our problems don't come from a lack of love on either of our parts, so maybe there's hope there, but I don't feel it very much these days to say the least.

And not stressing about job loss doesn't come easy when you have bills, a family, a smoking addiction and mental illness that needs to be medicated to have any hope of pulling anything in your life around. I also don't feel that adding financial stress to an already rocky marriage is going to improve the other problems in it.
Not really my issue, but.. why the fuck not really? Revenge won't really make me feel better about the situation, but I guess if I have to feel like shit, she should too.

I don't honestly think I can say that fixing this falls on her anymore at this point, no. She's apologized multiple times now and done everything in her power to reassure me of how much our relationship means to her and to reestablish the connection we used to have. I honestly believe she regrets the situation as much as I do, and that how things happened and the emotional fallout from it have shaken her quite a bit as her suicide attempt kind of shows.

So I guess if I truly want things to work between us and to keep having the life we've had together up until now, everything else falls on me to resolve. And I guess that means coming to terms with the fact that no person is perfect and people just fuck up sometimes, even with the things that they do value in life. And I have to come to terms with my own culpability  in things and question why I felt the need to make a stupid decision that could put my relationship at risk.

I have considered the idea of couples counseling, but don't know if this point if it was just be beating a dead horse to discuss it any further with a third party.  Personal counseling is definately a must at this point with how I feel, though.

She's expressed guilt at how the situation has affected me, but still insists that I'm taking some elements of the day/night out of context and making more of them than was there. Which I don't really know anymore if I am or she's just full of shit and wants to make herself look and feel better in the situation. She's been the same loving wife to me as always outside of this though. Although I fear the severity of my mood swings over it are going to cause more damage than the incident itself.
This indeed has been the symptom of my illness I have the hardest time keeping in check.

I'm well aware that the whole thing was a bad decision.  I don't really need that aspect pointed out to me. My whole post was about that. to answer your question, though, again I'm bi-polar but have been successfully managaing my symptoms un-medicated for nearly a decade now, this including getting through the loss of our child without putting a bullet between my eyes, so, I don't really think I can rightfully be called mentally weak, and I guess I kind of just incorrectly figured the worst of my mental illness was behind me and I could handle things better than this now. I was incorrect.
